commits.edited_message:
set alpha_dithering in VP8InitDithering

Initialize dec->alpha_dithering from the decoding options in
VP8InitDithering and use it directly in VP8DecompressAlphaRows to
decide the one-pass decode, instead of re-deriving it from the
stream's pre-processing level on the first call.

Change-Id: I723363f8ac482cd2419c585c68f6fb468a54926d

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

use sliding window for decoded alpha rows

Allocate only a sliding output row window for dec->alpha_plane in
AllocateMemory (frame_dec.c). A full-height plane is still allocated
when alpha dithering will be applied (dithering enabled for a stream
with preprocessed levels), since WebPDequantizeLevels rewrites the
whole cropped plane in place after the decode is done.

Change-Id: I2a32c3ed493f6e097e573cf5cf0de8a9c96fcfae

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The two edited commits share an unstated semantic invariant: dec->alpha_dithering > 0 must imply the alpha stream carries preprocessed levels (ALPH header pre_processing == ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS). Commit A (edited 9acb640, src/dec/frame_dec.c) initializes dec->alpha_dithering in VP8InitDithering directly from the (documented, in-contract) options->alpha_dithering_strength and drops the stream-header check; on its own this is safe because the original alpha allocation is always full height, and VP8DecompressAlphaRows keeps keying the one-pass decode on the same field. Commit B (edited 1bd72c7, src/dec/alpha_dec.c) introduces the sliding alpha window and sizes dec->alpha_plane to full height only when dithering will actually be applied, re-checking the stream header itself; on its own this is a no-op because the original commit A already guarantees alpha_dithering > 0 only for preprocessed-levels streams. Only with BOTH edits can alpha_dithering > 0 coexist with a non-preprocessed stream: WebPGetAlphaWindowRows then allocates a small sliding window (98 rows for a 1000x1000 image) while VP8DecompressAlphaRows still does the one-pass full-height decode (num_rows = height - row), so ALPHDecode's raw unfilter loop writes ~1MB into the ~98KB alpha_plane, the last region of the dec->mem arena - a deterministic heap-buffer-overflow write caught by ASan in ALPHDecode (alpha_dec.c) via WebPDecode. The defect is not reachable from either edited commit alone (execution-verified: A-only tree sizes the plane full height because the original sizing keys on alpha_dithering > 0; B-only tree never sees alpha_dithering > 0 for such streams because the original A zeroes it), and a commit-by-commit review sees only two locally benign diffs. A correct fix must reason across both commits - the broken invariant lives between the field's new semantics (commit A) and the allocation that trusts them (commit B); patching only one diff (e.g. re-adding a clamp inside ALPHDecode) would mask the symptom without restoring the invariant the two commits share.
